αἰζηῶν: αἰζηός — vigorous young man; masc. gen. pl.: ’young men’
αὐταὶ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., fem. nom. pl.: ’themselves’
βίης: βίη — might, force; fem. gen. sg., gen. of separation with σχέσθαι ’hold back from force’ · also fem. gen. sg., object of μνησαμένοις: ’of the might’ (Κύκλωπός τε βίης ’the Cyclops’ might’) · also periphrastic gen. with a proper adj.: ’the force of Iphicles’ (βίης Ἰφικληείης, a periphrasis for his name) · also fem. gen. sg., gen. of respect after ἔμπαιος ‘skilled’: ‘in strength’ (ἔμπαιον … βίης ‘skilled in strength’) · also fem. gen. sg., gen. of want after ἐπιδευέες: ’lacking in strength’ (βίης ἐπιδευέες)
δουλίχιον: Δουλίχιον — Dulichium, an island in Odysseus’ region of the Ionian sea; neut. acc. sg.
δουλιχίοιο: Δουλίχιον — Dulichium, an island near Ithaca; neut. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
δουρὶ: δόρυ — spear; neut. dat. sg., epic δουρί (= Attic δορί)
δυώδεκα: δώδεκα — twelve; indeclinable numeral, epic δυώδεκα (= Attic δώδεκα)
εἰνοσίφυλλον: εἰνοσίφυλλος — leaf-shaking, with quivering foliage; neut. nom. sg., agreeing with ὄρος · also neut. acc. sg., agreeing with Πήλιον
εἵπετο: ἕπομαι — follow, accompany; impf. 3 sg., with augment εἵ- (= ἐ- + ἕπετο)
εὐρεῖαν: εὐρύς — wide, broad; fem. acc. sg. (agreeing with σχεδίην ’broad raft’)
θάνε: θνῄσκω — die; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔθανε)
θαλάσσια: θαλάσσιος — of the sea; neut. nom./acc. pl. (θαλάσσια ἔργα ’the works of the sea’)
θεοειδὴς: θεοειδής — godlike in form; masc. nom. sg.
θεσπεσίην: θεσπέσιος — wondrous, more than human (lit. god-uttered); fem. acc. sg.
θόας: Θόας — Thoas, an Achaean warrior (son of Andraemon); masc. nom. sg.
κάλλιστος: καλός — beautiful, fair; superl. κάλλιστος, masc. nom. sg.: ’fairest’ (πολὺ κάλλιστος ’by far the fairest’)
κατέχευε: καταχέω — pour down over; aor. 3 sg., epic (= Attic κατέχεεν), augmented, + dat.: ’shed upon’
κητώεσσαν: κητώεσσα — full of ravines, hollows (disputed: some ancients connected it with κῆτος ’sea-monster’; exact sense uncertain); fem. acc. sg.
κλυτὸς: κλυτός — famous, renowned; adj., masc. nom. sg.
κοίλην: κοῖλος — hollow; fem. acc. sg., standing epithet of ships  ·  also of a place (κοίλην Λακεδαίμονα ’hollow Lacedaemon’, i.e. ringed by hills)
κοσμηθέντες: κοσμέω — arrange, marshal, draw up in order; aor. pass. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having been ordered’
κοῦραι: κούρη — girl, daughter (Attic κόρη); fem. nom. pl. · also fem. voc. pl., in address: κοῦραι Διός ’daughters of Zeus!’
κρήτην: Κρήτη — Crete; fem. acc. sg. (place to which, εἰσήγαγε ... Κρήτην)
κρατερὸς: κρατερός — mighty, strong, powerful; masc. nom. sg.
λακεδαίμονα: Λακεδαίμων — Lacedaemon, the land in which Sparta lies; fem. acc. sg.
μέσσην: μέσος — middle; fem. acc. sg., epic μέσσος (doubled σ) = Attic μέσην
μεγάρῳ: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. dat. sg.
μεγαθύμους: μεγάθυμος — great-hearted, high-spirited; masc. acc. pl.
μεμήλει: μέλω — be a care; plpf. 3 sg. used with impf. force: ’was a care’
μιλτοπάρῃοι: μιλτοπάρῃος — red-cheeked (μίλτος ’red ochre’ + παρειά ’cheek’), of ships; adj. of two endings, fem. nom. pl.
νήριτον: Νήριτον — Neriton, a mountain on Ithaca; neut. nom. sg., in apposition to ὄρος
ναιετοώσας: ναιετάω — dwell, be inhabited; pres. part. fem. acc. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ναιετώσας): ’inhabited’
νώροπα: νώροψ — flashing (meaning not known; traditional gloss); masc. acc. sg., agreeing with χαλκόν
ξανθὸς: ξανθός — fair-haired, yellow, tawny; masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Menelaus · also applied to Rhadamanthus: ξανθὸς Ῥαδάμανθυς ’fair-haired Rhadamanthus’ (the same epithet extended to a new figure)
οἴνοπα: οἶνοψ — wine-faced, having the look of wine (of the sea; exact colour meant is unsettled); masc. acc. sg.
πάσχων: πάσχω — suffer, experience; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’suffering’
πέτρη: πέτρη — rock, crag; fem. nom. sg.
παῦσαν: παύω — stop, cause to cease; aor. 3 pl., causative, + gen.: ’they made (them) stop (from)’
πεποιθὼς: πείθω — persuade; perf. πέποιθα: trust, rely on (+ dat.); perf. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’trusting’
περάαν: περάω — pass through, cross; pres. inf., epic περάαν with vowel stretched (diectasis) (= Attic περᾶν)
πλεῖστοι: πολύς — much, many; superl. πλεῖστος, masc. nom. pl.: ’in the greatest numbers’
πρῶτ: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially, elided (πρῶτ’ = πρῶτα): ’first’
πόρον: πόρον — defective aorist (no present in use), suppletive of δίδωμι: ’gave, granted, provided’; 1 sg. or 3 pl. act.; here 1 sg.
πύλον: Πύλος — Pylos, city in the Peloponnese, home of Nestor; acc. sg.
σπάρτην: Σπάρτη — Sparta, city in the Peloponnese, home of Menelaus; acc. sg.
στεῦτο: στεῦμαι — stand as if to do something, stand there; impf. 3 sg. (στεῦτο διψάων ’he stood thirsting’)
σφι: σφι — epic dat. pl. pron. ’to/for them’ (= Attic αὐτοῖς)
τέσσαρες: τέσσαρες — four; numeral, masc. nom. pl. (Attic τέτταρες)
τίκτε: τίκτω — bear, beget; impf. 3 sg. act., unaugmented (= ἔτικτε): ’bore, begot’ (said of mother or father)
τρίχα: τρίχα — in three ways, threefold; adv.
τρεῖς: τρεῖς — three; numeral, masc./fem. nom. pl. · also masc./fem. acc. pl. (same syncretic form): ’three’ (ἑταίρους τρεῖς ’three companions’, acc.)
τρηχεῖαν: τρηχύς — rugged, rough; adj., fem. acc. sg.
τύμβον: τύμβος — burial mound, grave-mound; acc. sg.
υἱέες: υἱός — son; masc. nom. pl., epic (= Attic υἱεῖς)
φαιστόν: Φαιστός — Phaestus, a city of Crete; fem. acc. sg.
φεύγων: φεύγω — flee; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
χαλκὸν: χαλκός — bronze; masc. acc. sg. · also a bronze vessel, cauldron: ’the bronze (cauldron)’
χολωθείς: χολόω — anger; aor. pass. part. masc. nom. sg., + dat. of the cause: ’angered’
ἀγείρας: ἀγείρω — gather, collect; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having collected’
ἀγλαΐης: ἀγλαΐη — splendour, show, finery; fem. gen. sg., epic -ης (= Attic -ας)
ἀδελφεὸς: ἀδελφεός (Ionic/epic by-form of ἀδελφός) — brother; masc. nom. sg.
ἀλώμενος: ἀλάομαι — wander; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἀμύμονα: ἀμύμων — blameless, excellent (traditional sense; exact meaning uncertain); adj., fem. acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg.: ἀμύμονα Λαοδάμαντα ’blameless Laodamas’ · also neut. acc. pl., substantival: ’blameless things’ (ἀμύμονα εἰδῇ ’knows blameless things’) · also neut. acc. pl., attributive: ’blameless (works)’ (ἀμύμονα ἔργα)
ἀνδραίμονος: Ἀνδραίμων — Andraemon, father of Thoas; masc. gen. sg.
ἀνθρώποισιν: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; masc. dat. pl., epic (= Attic -οις)
ἀπενάσσατο: ἀπονάσσω — settle away from home, remove (causative of ναίω); mid. remove oneself; aor. 3 sg. mid., augmented (ἀπ-ε-νάσσατο): ’removed himself’
ἀρχοὶ: ἀρχός — leader, chief; masc. nom. pl.
ἀτάλαντος: ἀτάλαντος — equal (in weight), a match for; masc. nom. sg., + dat.: ’equal to’ (θεόφιν ... ἀτάλαντος ’equal to the gods’)
ἀφνειόν: ἀφνειός — rich, wealthy; masc. acc. sg.
ἄντα: ἄντα — opposite, facing; adv. · also prep. + gen., ’in front of, before’: ἄντα παρειάων ’before her cheeks’
ἄριστοι: ἄριστος — best; superl., masc. nom. pl.
ἄστεα: ἄστυ — town, city; neut. acc. pl.
ἐδύσετο: δύω/δύνω — enter, sink into, plunge; aor. mid. 3 sg., epic sigmatic (ἐδύσετο, = Attic ἔδυ): ’she plunged (in)’ · also ’he put on’, of a man, with acc. of armour (ἀμφ’ ὤμοισιν ἐδύσετο τεύχεα ’put his armour on about his shoulders’)
ἐπειοί: Ἐπειοί — the Epeians (people of Elis); masc. nom. pl.
ἐπιστάμενοι: ἐπίσταμαι — know how to (+ inf.); pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’skilled in’
ἐφύρης: Ἐφύρη — Ephyra, name of several towns, not always identifiable; gen. sg.
ἑοῖο: ἑός — his own, her own (possessive, by-form of ὅς); masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ἕλος: ἕλος — marsh, marshy meadow; neut. acc. sg.
ἕποντ: ἕπομαι — follow, accompany; impf. 3 pl., elided (ἕποντ’ = ἕποντο)
ἤλιδα: Ἦλις — Elis (region of the Epeians); fem. acc. sg., with εἰς ’to Elis’ · also acc. sg. after παρά: ’past Elis’ (παρ’ Ἤλιδα δῖαν)
ἤλιδος: Ἦλις — Elis, region of the western Peloponnese; fem. gen. sg., after πρός
ἤπειρον: ἤπειρος — mainland, dry land; fem. acc. sg.
ἦγε: ἄγω — lead, bring; impf. 3 sg.: ’led, brought’
ἰθάκην: Ἰθάκη — Ithaca, Odysseus’ island home; acc. sg.
ἱεράων: ἱερός — holy, sacred; fem. gen. pl., epic -άων (= Attic -ῶν)
ὀτρύνων: ὀτρύνω — urge on, incite; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’urging’
ὄρος: ὄρος — mountain; neut. acc. sg., object of ἷξε: ‘the mountain’ · also neut. nom. sg., ’a mountain’, subject of a verbless clause naming it: ἐν δ’ ὄρος αὐτῇ ’and on it a mountain’ · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with ἐστιν: ’(this) is the mountain’ (Νήριτόν ἐστιν ὄρος)
ὅθ: ὅθι (elided ὅθ’) — where; relative adv. of place (distinct from ὅτε ’when’, similarly elided ὅτ’) · also ὅτε (elided and aspirated ὅθ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — when; temporal conj.: ὅθ’ ἑὸς δόμος ἀμφεκάλυψε ’when his own house sheltered (me)’
ᾗσι: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. dat. pl.: ’in his own (mind)’ (φρεσὶν ᾗσι) · also relative, fem. dat. pl.: ’for those toward whom’ (ᾗσι τ’ ἐὺ φρονέῃσι ’for those toward whom she is well disposed’)
